meaning.zh:
“被解雇” 或 “被开除”。

这个短语起源于军事用语，指士兵被允许离开营地或岗位时会接到一份行军证或许可以称作 “行军令”。逐渐地，这个表达被引入到职场用语，用来表示因为某人被解雇而收到的解雇通知。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from a military context, where soldiers would receive "walking papers" or a leave pass permitting them to leave the camp or post. Over time, this expression was adopted in the workplace to signify being given a termination notice.

lines.en: After the company downsized, a lot of employees got their *walking papers*.
lines.zh: 公司裁员后，许多员工被解雇了。

lines.en: Tom was late for work too many times and finally got his *walking papers*.
lines.zh: 汤姆上班迟到了太多次，最终被解雇了。

lines.en: I heard that if sales don’t improve, some of us might get our *walking papers*.
lines.zh: 我听说如果销售业绩不改善，我们中的一些人可能会被解雇。
